Confirming PET computaiton method:- choice between Hargraves and Thornthwaite

## PET computation 
PET_hargreaves <- hargreaves(Tmin = monthly_tbl$Tmin,Tmax = monthly_tbl$Tmax,Pre = monthly_tbl$prec,lat = 53.6332)
## [1] "Calculating reference evapotranspiration using the Hargreaves method. Using latitude (`lat`) to estimate extraterrestrial radiation. Using precipitation data, following Droogers and Allen (2002). Checking for missing values (`NA`): all the data must be complete. Input type is vector. Assuming the data are monthly time series starting in January, all regular (non-leap) years."
PET_thornthwaite <- thornthwaite(Tave = monthly_tbl$Tavg,lat = 53.6332)
## [1] "Checking for missing values (`NA`): all the data must be complete. Input type is vector. Assuming the data are monthly time series starting in January, all regular (non-leap) years."

We select Hargreaves

Key Observations from Your Data:

Thornthwaite shows many zero values - This is problematic as it indicates the method fails during winter months when temperatures are low Hargreaves provides continuous values - More realistic for year-round analysis Hargreaves generally shows higher PET values - This is typical for coastal areas

Recommendation for Hamburg Fühlsbuttel: Use Hargreaves method for the following reasons: Climate-Specific Advantages:

Coastal location: Hargreaves performs better in maritime climates like Hamburg Temperature range: Better suited for the moderate temperature variations in northern Germany Humidity considerations: While it doesn’t directly use humidity, it’s calibrated for regions with moderate humidity

Technical Advantages:

No zero values: Ensures continuous drought index calculation Widely validated: Extensively tested in European climates Robust performance: Less sensitive to extreme temperature variations

For Your Location Specifically:

Hamburg’s maritime climate (Köppen Cfb) is well-suited for Hargreaves The method works well for locations with moderate temperature ranges (like northern Germany) Less prone to computational issues in winter

Selecting Hargraves for the Computation of PET

monthly_tbl <- monthly_tbl |>

  rename(PREC = prec)
## [1] "Calculating reference evapotranspiration using the Hargreaves method. Using latitude (`lat`) to estimate extraterrestrial radiation. Using precipitation data, following Droogers and Allen (2002). Checking for missing values (`NA`): all the data must be complete. Input type is vector. Assuming the data are monthly time series starting in January, all regular (non-leap) years."

Drought Indices:-

Reconnaissance Drought Index (RDI) :- Computation is as follows

# Computation function for RDI 
calculate_monthly_rdi <- function(data, scale) {
  require(dplyr)
  require(zoo)
  
  data <- data %>%
    arrange(date) %>%
    filter(PET > 0, PREC >= 0) %>%
    mutate(
      PREC_sum = rollsum(PREC, k = scale, fill = NA, align = "right"),
      PET_sum = rollsum(PET, k = scale, fill = NA, align = "right"),
      alpha = ifelse(PET_sum > 0, PREC_sum / PET_sum, NA_real_)
    )
  
  valid_alphas <- data$alpha[!is.na(data$alpha) & is.finite(data$alpha) & data$alpha > 0]
  
  if (length(valid_alphas) > 30) {
    log_alphas <- log(valid_alphas)
    y_bar <- mean(log_alphas, na.rm = TRUE)
    sigma_y <- sd(log_alphas, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    data <- data %>%
      mutate(
        RDIst = ifelse(alpha > 0, (log(alpha) - y_bar) / sigma_y, NA_real_)
      )
  } else {
    data$RDIst <- NA_real_
  }
  
  # Only return date and RDIst
  return(data |>  dplyr::select(date, RDIst))
}
# Funciton for differrent scales
calculate_rdist_for_scales <- function(data, scales = c(3,6,9,12,24,36,48)) {
  require(dplyr)
  
  result <- data |> dplyr:: select(date)  # Start with date column
  
  for (k in scales) {
    rdi_k <- calculate_monthly_rdi(data, scale = k) %>%
      rename(!!paste0("RDI_", k) := RDIst)
    
    result <- left_join(result, rdi_k, by = "date")
  }
  
  return(result)
}


monthly_rdist_tbl <- calculate_rdist_for_scales(data = monthly_tbl)

We have 3,6,9,12,24,36,48 monthly scale. So then which scales are important for the analysis. Since the period is 1936-2025, so 3,6,9 scales will not be that informative as these will refelect very short term changes. So 12,24,36,48 are better choices

RDI 12 1936-1989

rdi_12tbl <- monthly_rdist_tbl |> 
  dplyr::select(date,RDI_12) |> 
  drop_na()

rdi_12tbl <- rdi_12tbl |> 
  dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(RDI_12 >0,"pos","neg")) |> 
# Enhanced data preparation with drought categories
 dplyr:: mutate(
    # Original sign classification
    sign = ifelse(RDI_12 > 0, "pos", "neg"),
    
    drought_category = case_when(
      RDI_12 >= 2.0 ~ "Extremely Wet",
      RDI_12 >= 1.5 & RDI_12 < 2.0 ~ "Very Wet", 
      RDI_12 >= 1.0 & RDI_12 < 1.5 ~ "Moderately Wet",
      RDI_12 >= 0.5 & RDI_12 < 1.0 ~ "Slightly Wet",
      RDI_12 >= -0.5 & RDI_12 < 0.5 ~ "Normal",
      RDI_12 >= -1.0 & RDI_12 < -0.5 ~ "Mild Drought",
      RDI_12 >= -1.5 & RDI_12 < -1.0 ~ "Moderate Drought",
      RDI_12 >= -2.0 & RDI_12 < -1.5 ~ "Severe Drought",
      TRUE ~ "Extreme Drought"  # RDI_12 < -2.0
    ),
    
    # Create ordered factor for proper legend ordering
    drought_category = factor(drought_category, levels = c(
      "Extreme Drought", "Severe Drought", "Moderate Drought", 
      "Mild Drought", "Normal", "Slightly Wet", 
      "Moderately Wet", "Very Wet", "Extremely Wet"
    ))
  )
rdi_12tbl <- rdi_12tbl |> filter(date <="1989-12-01")


# Calculate key statistics for plot annotations
drought_stats <- rdi_12tbl |>
  summarise(
    total_months = n(),
    drought_months = sum(RDI_12 < -0.5),
    severe_drought_months = sum(RDI_12 < -1.5),
    wet_months = sum(RDI_12 > 0.5),
    min_rdi = min(RDI_12),
    max_rdi = max(RDI_12),
    min_date = date[which.min(RDI_12)],
    max_date = date[which.max(RDI_12)],
    drought_pct = round(drought_months / total_months * 100, 2),
    severe_drought_pct = round(severe_drought_months / total_months * 100, 2),
    wet_pct = round(wet_months / total_months * 100, 1)
  )

# Create statistical summary for subtitle
stats_text <- paste0(
  "Drought conditions: ", drought_stats$drought_pct, "% | ",
  "Severe drought: ", drought_stats$severe_drought_pct, "% | ",
  "Wet events: ", drought_stats$wet_pct, "% | ",
  "Wettest: ", format(drought_stats$max_date, "%b %Y"), " (", round(drought_stats$max_rdi, 2), ") | ",
  "Driest: ", format(drought_stats$min_date, "%b %Y"), " (", round(drought_stats$min_rdi, 2), ")"
)

# Define color palette for drought categories
drought_colors <- c(
  "Extreme Drought" = "#8B0000",     # Dark Red
  "Severe Drought" = "#FF0000",      # Red  
  "Moderate Drought" = "#FF4500",    # Orange Red
  "Mild Drought" = "#FFA500",        # Orange
  "Normal" = "#CCCCCC",              # Light Gray
  "Slightly Wet" = "#87CEEB",        # Sky Blue
  "Moderately Wet" = "#4682B4",      # Steel Blue
  "Very Wet" = "#1E90FF",            # Dodger Blue
  "Extremely Wet" = "#0000CD"        # Medium Blue
)

           size = 4.5, hjust = 0, color = "#8B0000", fontface = "bold") +

  # Start and End Labels (adjusted positioning)

🧾 Summary Statement Between 1936 and 1989, Hamburg experienced a relatively wet-dominant climate with fewer droughts and more frequent moisture surpluses. While Extreme droughts such as the 1959 drought (RDI -3.9) and the 1981 wet event (RDI 2.7) did occur, overall drought conditions were less intense and less frequent compared to the post-1990 period. This era serves as a hydroclimatic baseline, highlighting the shift toward drier and more variable conditions in the modern climate.

    ))

Historical Climate Characteristics (1936-2025)

Overall Water Balance:

Hamburg experiences a slightly wet-biased climate - wet events (29.8%) are more common than drought conditions (25.4%) Normal conditions dominate (~45% of the time) Severe droughts are relatively rare (only 7.2% of the period)

Major Climate Periods Identified 1940s-1950s: The Dry Era

Sustained drought conditions, culminating in the extreme drought of October 1959 (RDI: -3.9) This was the driest period in Hamburg’s modern record

1960s-1980s: The Wet Period

Markedly wetter conditions with frequent positive RDI values Peak wetness in May 1981 (RDI: 2.7) - the wettest event on record This represents a major climate shift from the previous dry period

1990s-Present: Increased Variability

More volatile conditions with alternating wet/dry cycles Notable drought events in early 2000s, around 2018-2020 Suggests potentially changing climate patterns

Climate Resilience Insights Natural Variability:

Hamburg’s climate shows strong decadal-scale oscillations Extreme droughts (both wet and dry) are part of the natural system The city has historically recovered from severe droughts

Water Security:

3 out of 4 years have adequate to excess moisture Severe water stress is infrequent but can be prolonged when it occurs The 1950s drought lasted several years, showing persistence is possible

Implications for Planning Infrastructure & Water Management:

Design systems to handle RDI values from -4 to +3 Plan for drought events that could last 2-3 years (like 1950s pattern) Expect wet periods that could cause flooding concerns

Agriculture & Ecosystems:

Hamburg’s ecosystems are adapted to this wet-dry variability Crop planning should account for roughly 1-in-4 chance of drought conditions Irrigation needs are moderate compared to more arid regions

Climate Change Context:

Recent decades show increasing volatility rather than a clear trend toward wetter/drier The question is whether future extremes will exceed the historical -4 to +3 range Current variability may be the “new normal” rather than transitional

Bottom Line Hamburg has a naturally variable but generally water-secure climate with distinct multi-decadal wet and dry phases. While severe droughts occur, they’re historically followed by recovery periods. The main concern for the future may be increased unpredictability rather than systematic drying or wetting.

Metric 1936–1989 1990–2025 1936–2025
Drought Conditions 23.5% of months 28.2% ↑ 25.4% of months
Severe Drought Conditions 6.8% of months 7.8% ↑ 7.2% of months
Wet Events 31.7% of months 27.1% ↓ 29.8% of months
Wettest Event May 1981 (RDI: 2.7) May 1994 (RDI: 2.6) May 1981 (RDI: 2.7)
Driest Event Oct 1959 (RDI: -3.9) Jan 2019 (RDI: -3.0) Oct 1959 (RDI: -3.9)

🌡️ Shift Toward More Drought-Prone Conditions Drought conditions increased to 28.2% of months, up from 25.4% historically.

Severe droughts rose to 7.8%, compared to 7.2% in the full-period record.

Wet events declined to 27.1%, down from 29.8% during 1936–2025.

➡️ Implication: Hamburg’s climate has become slightly more drought-prone in recent decades, with increasing frequency and intensity of dry conditions.

📉 New Extremes and Reduced Wet Surpluses Driest event: January 2019 (RDI: -3.0) — most severe drought of the modern period.

Wettest event: May 1994 (RDI: 2.6) — strong but slightly below the 1981 historical maximum (RDI: 2.7).

No wet events above +2.7 RDI observed since 1981.

➡️ Implication: While extreme wet events have diminished in intensity, extreme droughts still occur, and their frequency is increasing.

🔁 Changing Balance in Climate Variability The modern RDI distribution is nearly balanced:

28.2% drought vs. 27.1% wet events.

In contrast, the historical period showed a wet bias (29.8% wet vs. 25.4% drought).

The absence of extremely wet years after 1994 suggests a loss of moisture surplus periods.

➡️ Implication: The long-term wet-dominated climate is giving way to a more neutral or drought-inclined regime.

🧠 Interpretation and Trends 1. Drought Intensification The rise in both total and severe drought occurrences during 1990–2025 highlights a shift toward more persistent and impactful dry spells, consistent with warming-related hydroclimatic stress.

  1. Persistence and Clustering Clusters of droughts, particularly in the early 2000s and 2015–2020, point to multi-year drought patterns rather than isolated events.

  2. Declining Wet Extremes No extremely wet events exceeding RDI > 2.7 occurred post-1981, indicating that extreme recharge periods have not matched past levels.

  3. Modern Drought Benchmark The 2019 drought (RDI: -3.0) serves as a new benchmark for planning and adaptation, nearly matching the legendary 1959 drought (RDI: -3.9).

📌 Climate Change Implications for Hamburg Evidence of Regime Shift: More frequent droughts.

Fewer, less intense wet events.

Balanced but more variable hydroclimate.

Possible Drivers: Weakened Atlantic (maritime) moisture influence.

Increased continentality, favoring drier extremes.

🛠️ Practical Recommendations Water resource planning should be based on a 28% drought frequency, not the outdated 25%.

The 2019 drought should be used as a realistic extreme scenario in infrastructure and policy assessments.

Agriculture and ecosystems must be managed with the expectation of symmetrical risk of both drought and wet periods — unlike the past wet-dominated conditions.

Bottom Line Between 1990 and 2025, Hamburg has transitioned from a historically wet-biased climate to a more drought-sensitive one. The rising frequency of dry conditions and absence of extreme wet years underline the need for updated climate adaptation strategies.

      TRUE ~ "Extreme Drought"  # RDI_24 < -2.0

    # Create ordered factor for proper legend ordering

      "Extreme Drought", "Severe Drought", "Moderate Drought",

# Create RDI table and classify
rdi_24tbl <- monthly_rdist_tbl |> 
  dplyr::select(date, RDI_24) |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  mutate(
    sign = ifelse(RDI_24 > 0, "pos", "neg"),
    drought_category = case_when(
      RDI_24 >= 2.0 ~ "Extremely Wet",
      RDI_24 >= 1.5 ~ "Very Wet", 
      RDI_24 >= 1.0 ~ "Moderately Wet",
      RDI_24 >= 0.5 ~ "Slightly Wet",
      RDI_24 >= -0.5 ~ "Normal",
      RDI_24 >= -1.0 ~ "Mild Drought",
      RDI_24 >= -1.5 ~ "Moderate Drought",
      RDI_24 >= -2.0 ~ "Severe Drought",
      TRUE ~ "Extreme Drought"
    ),
    drought_category = factor(drought_category, levels = c(
      "Extreme Drought", "Severe Drought", "Moderate Drought", 
      "Mild Drought", "Normal", "Slightly Wet", 
      "Moderately Wet", "Very Wet", "Extremely Wet"
    ))
  )

# Compute statistics
drought_stats <- rdi_24tbl |> summarise(
  total_months = n(),
  drought_months = sum(RDI_24 < -0.5),
  severe_drought_months = sum(RDI_24 < -1.5),
  wet_months = sum(RDI_24 > 0.5),
  min_rdi = min(RDI_24),
  max_rdi = max(RDI_24),
  min_date = date[which.min(RDI_24)],
  max_date = date[which.max(RDI_24)],
  drought_pct = round(drought_months / total_months * 100, 1),
  severe_drought_pct = round(severe_drought_months / total_months * 100, 1),
  wet_pct = round(wet_months / total_months * 100, 1)
)

# Prepare dynamic text
stats_text <- paste0(
  "Drought conditions: ", drought_stats$drought_pct, "% | ",
  "Severe drought: ", drought_stats$severe_drought_pct, "% | ",
  " Wet events : ", drought_stats$wet_pct, "%|",
  "Wettest: ", format(drought_stats$max_date, "%b %Y"), " (", round(drought_stats$max_rdi, 1), ") | ",
  "Driest: ", format(drought_stats$min_date, "%b %Y"), " (", round(drought_stats$min_rdi, 1), ")"
)

# Define color palette
drought_colors <- c(
  "Extreme Drought" = "#8B0000",
  "Severe Drought" = "#FF0000",
  "Moderate Drought" = "#FF4500",
  "Mild Drought" = "#FFA500",
  "Normal" = "#CCCCCC",
  "Slightly Wet" = "#87CEEB",
  "Moderately Wet" = "#4682B4",

  "Extremely Wet" = "#0000CD"
)

# Define dynamic x-axis and annotation window

mid_date <- mean(as.numeric(date_range)) |> as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01")

p10

Inference and Analysis: The 12-month RDI analysis for Hamburg Fuhlsbüttel from 1990 to 2025 reveals a shifting pattern in annual drought dynamics. While the early 1990s experienced substantial wet conditions—including the wettest period in May 1994 (RDI = 2.6)—recent decades have seen more frequent and intense droughts, culminating in the Extreme drought of January 2019 (RDI = -3.0). Overall, 28.2% of the period was marked by drought (RDI < -0.5), and 7.8% experienced severe drought (RDI < -1.5), indicating a significant increase in water stress risk, particularly in the last decade. These findings emphasize the importance of ongoing monitoring and adaptation strategies, especially in light of potential climate-driven shifts in hydrological cycles.

Interpretation & Analysis

The 24-month RDI trend for Hamburg Fuhlsbüttel from 1990 to 2024 reveals significant interannual variability in drought and wet conditions. While early decades (especially the 1990s) showed frequent and intense wet periods, the most recent decade has been characterized by prolonged dry conditions, culminating in the driest month observed in January 2020 (RDI = -2.4). Overall, drought conditions were present during 37.6% of the study period, with 4.7% classified as severe. This indicates increasing susceptibility to long-term water stress, especially post-2010.

    ),
    
    # Create ordered factor for proper legend ordering
    drought_category = factor(drought_category, levels = c(

      "Moderately Wet", "Very Wet", "Extremely Wet"
    ))
  ) |> filter(date<"1990-01-01")

# Calculate key statistics for plot annotations
drought_stats <- rdi_36tbl |>
  summarise(
    total_months = n(),
    drought_months = sum(RDI_36 < -0.5),
    severe_drought_months = sum(RDI_36 < -1.5),
    wet_months = sum(RDI_36 > 0.5),
    min_rdi = min(RDI_36),
    max_rdi = max(RDI_36),
    min_date = date[which.min(RDI_36)],
    max_date = date[which.max(RDI_36)],
    drought_pct = round(drought_months / total_months * 100, 1),
    severe_drought_pct = round(severe_drought_months / total_months * 100, 1),
    wet_pct = round(wet_months / total_months * 100, 1)
  )

# Create statistical summary for subtitle
stats_text <- paste0(
  "Drought conditions: ", drought_stats$drought_pct, "% | ",
  "Severe drought: ", drought_stats$severe_drought_pct, "% | ",
  "Wet events: ",drought_stats$wet_pct, "% | ",
  "Wettest: ", format(drought_stats$max_date, "%b %Y"), " (", round(drought_stats$max_rdi, 1), ") | ",
  "Driest: ", format(drought_stats$min_date, "%b %Y"), " (", round(drought_stats$min_rdi, 1), ")"
)

# Define color palette for drought categories
drought_colors <- c(
  "Extreme Drought" = "#8B0000",     # Dark Red
  "Severe Drought" = "#FF0000",      # Red  
  "Moderate Drought" = "#FF4500",    # Orange Red
  "Mild Drought" = "#FFA500",        # Orange
  "Normal" = "#CCCCCC",              # Light Gray
  "Slightly Wet" = "#87CEEB",        # Sky Blue
  "Moderately Wet" = "#4682B4",      # Steel Blue
  "Very Wet" = "#1E90FF",            # Dodger Blue
  "Extremely Wet" = "#0000CD"        # Medium Blue
)

# Define dynamic x-axis and annotation window
date_range <- range(rdi_36tbl$date)
mid_date <- mean(as.numeric(date_range)) |> as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01")
annotation_start <- mid_date %m-% years(20)
annotation_end <- mid_date %m-% years(4)

# Plot
p31 <- ggplot(rdi_36tbl, aes(x = date, y = RDI_36, fill = drought_category)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = TRUE, width = 20) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = seq(-2, 2, 0.5), 
             color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = drought_stats$min_date, color = "#8B0000", linetype = "dotdash", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = drought_stats$max_date, color = "#00008B", linetype = "dotdash", linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Annotation box
  annotate("rect", xmin = annotation_start , xmax = annotation_end,
           ymin = 2.5, ymax = 3.5, fill = "white", color = "grey60", alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = annotation_start, y = 3.35, 
           label = paste0("KEY INSIGHTS (", year(date_range[1]) - 4, "-", year(date_range[2]), ")"),
           size = 5, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = annotation_start, y = 3.15, 
           label = paste0("• Drought conditions: ", drought_stats$drought_pct, "%"),
           size = 5, hjust = 0, color = "#CC0000") +
  annotate("text", x = annotation_start, y = 2.9, 
           label = paste0("• Severe drought: ", drought_stats$severe_drought_pct, "%"),
           size = 5, hjust = 0, color = "#8B0000", fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = annotation_start, y = 2.65, 
           label = paste0("• Wet Events: ", drought_stats$wet_pct, "%"),
           size = 5, hjust = 0, color = "#00008B", fontface = "bold") +

  # Labels for events
  annotate("label", x = drought_stats$min_date, y = drought_stats$min_rdi,
           label = paste0("Extreme Drought: ", format(drought_stats$min_date, "%b %Y"),
                          " (RDI: ", round(drought_stats$min_rdi, 2), ")"),
           fill = "#8B0000", color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 4, label.size = NA, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("label", x = drought_stats$max_date, y = drought_stats$max_rdi,
           label = paste0("Wettest Event: ", format(drought_stats$max_date, "%b %Y"),
                          " (RDI: ", round(drought_stats$max_rdi, 2), ")"),
           fill = "#00008B", color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5, label.size = NA, hjust = 1) +

  # Start/End labels
  annotate("text", x = date_range[1], y = 3, 
           label = "Start of analysis", hjust = 1, size = 5, color = "grey40", fontface = "bold",angle = 90) +
  annotate("text", x = date_range[2], y = 3, 
           label = "End of analysis", hjust = 1, size = 5, color = "grey50", fontface = "bold", angle = 90) +

  # Scales
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "5 years",
    date_labels = "%Y",
    limits = c(as.Date("1936-01-01"),as.Date("1990-01-01")),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-2.5, 3.5),
    breaks = seq(-2.5, 3.5, 0.5),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Condition",
    values = drought_colors,
    guide = guide_legend(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      nrow = 1,
      reverse = TRUE
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Drought Severity in Hamburg Fuhlsbüttel(1936-1989)",
    subtitle = paste0("RDI (36-Month Scale)|",stats_text),
    caption = "Source: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 22, margin = margin(t = 10, b = 15)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey60", size = 16, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey60", size = 15, hjust = 1, margin = margin(t = 20)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 18, colour = "grey10", face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 18, colour = "gray10", face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14,face = "bold"),
    legend.key.size = unit(.5, "cm")
  )

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(plot_dir, "RDI_36_Monthly_1936_1989.png"),
  plot = p31,
  width = 15,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 450
)

RDI 48 (1990-2025)

rdi_48tbl <- monthly_rdist_tbl |> 
  dplyr::select(date, RDI_48) |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  filter(date >= "1990-01-01") |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Original sign classification
    sign = ifelse(RDI_48 > 0, "pos", "neg"),
    
    drought_category = case_when(
      RDI_48 >= 2.0 ~ "Extremely Wet",
      RDI_48 >= 1.5 & RDI_48 < 2.0 ~ "Very Wet", 
      RDI_48 >= 1.0 & RDI_48 < 1.5 ~ "Moderately Wet",
      RDI_48 >= 0.5 & RDI_48 < 1.0 ~ "Slightly Wet",
      RDI_48 >= -0.5 & RDI_48 < 0.5 ~ "Normal",
      RDI_48 >= -1.0 & RDI_48 < -0.5 ~ "Mild Drought",
      RDI_48 >= -1.5 & RDI_48 < -1.0 ~ "Moderate Drought",
      RDI_48 >= -2.0 & RDI_48 < -1.5 ~ "Severe Drought",
      TRUE ~ "Extreme Drought"  # RDI_48 < -2.0
    ),
    
    # Create ordered factor for proper legend ordering
    drought_category = factor(drought_category, levels = c(
      "Extreme Drought", "Severe Drought", "Moderate Drought", 
      "Mild Drought", "Normal", "Slightly Wet", 
      "Moderately Wet", "Very Wet", "Extremely Wet"
    ))
  )

# Calculate key statistics for plot annotations
drought_stats <- rdi_48tbl |>
  summarise(
    total_months = n(),
    drought_months = sum(RDI_48 < -0.5),
    severe_drought_months = sum(RDI_48 < -1.5),
    wet_months = sum(RDI_48 > 0.5),
    min_rdi = min(RDI_48),
    max_rdi = max(RDI_48),
    min_date = date[which.min(RDI_48)],
    max_date = date[which.max(RDI_48)],
    drought_pct = round(drought_months / total_months * 100, 1),
    severe_drought_pct = round(severe_drought_months / total_months * 100, 1),
    wet_pct = round(wet_months / total_months * 100, 1)
  )

# Create statistical summary for subtitle
stats_text <- paste0(
  "Drought conditions: ", drought_stats$drought_pct, "% | ",
  "Severe drought: ", drought_stats$severe_drought_pct, "% | ",
   "Wet events: ", drought_stats$wet_pct, "% | ",
  "Wettest: ", format(drought_stats$max_date, "%b %Y"), " (", round(drought_stats$max_rdi, 1), ") | ",
  "Driest: ", format(drought_stats$min_date, "%b %Y"), " (", round(drought_stats$min_rdi, 1), ")"
)

# Define color palette for drought categories
drought_colors <- c(
  "Extreme Drought" = "#8B0000",     # Dark Red
  "Severe Drought" = "#FF0000",      # Red  
  "Moderate Drought" = "#FF4500",    # Orange Red
  "Mild Drought" = "#FFA500",        # Orange
  "Normal" = "#CCCCCC",              # Light Gray
  "Slightly Wet" = "#87CEEB",        # Sky Blue
  "Moderately Wet" = "#4682B4",      # Steel Blue
  "Very Wet" = "#1E90FF",            # Dodger Blue
  "Extremely Wet" = "#0000CD"        # Medium Blue
)

# Define dynamic x-axis and annotation window
date_range <- range(rdi_48tbl$date)
mid_date <- mean(as.numeric(date_range)) |> as.Date(origin = "1970-01-01")
annotation_start <- mid_date
annotation_end <- mid_date %m+% years(5)

p42 <- ggplot(rdi_48tbl, aes(x = date, y = RDI_48, fill = drought_category)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = TRUE, width = 20) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Add reference dashed lines
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-2, -1.5, -1, -0.5, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2), 
             color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.6) +

  # Highlight driest and wettest periods
  geom_vline(xintercept = drought_stats$min_date, color = "#8B0000", linetype = "dotdash", linewidth = 0.8) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = drought_stats$max_date, color = "#00008B", linetype = "dotdash", linewidth = 0.8) +

  # # KEY INSIGHTS annotation box
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = annotation_start, xmax = annotation_end,
           ymin = 2, ymax = 3,
           fill = "white", color = "grey60", alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.5) +

  annotate("text", x = annotation_start, y = 2.85,
         label = paste0("KEY INSIGHTS (", min(year(rdi_48tbl$date)), "-", max(year(rdi_48tbl$date)), ")"),
         size = 6, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0) +


  annotate("text", x = annotation_start, y = 2.65,
           label = paste0("• Drought conditions: ", drought_stats$drought_pct, "%"),
           size = 6, hjust = 0, color = "#CC0000") +

  annotate("text", x = annotation_start, y = 2.45,
           label = paste0("• Severe drought: ", drought_stats$severe_drought_pct, "%"),
           size = 6, hjust = 0, color = "#8B0000", fontface = "bold")  +
  annotate("text", x = annotation_start, y = 2.25, 
          label = paste0("• Wet Events: ", drought_stats$wet_pct, "%"),
            size = 6, hjust = 0, color = "#00008B", fontface = "bold") +

 
  
  annotate("label", 
         x = drought_stats$min_date, 
         y = -2.9,
         label = paste0(format(drought_stats$min_date, " %Y %b "), 
                        "Event Extreme (RDI: ", round(drought_stats$min_rdi, 1), ")"),
         fill = "#8B0000",              # Background color of the label
         size = 5, 
         hjust = 1, 
         color = "white",       
         fontface = "bold", label.size = NA ) +
         
  annotate("label", x = drought_stats$max_date, y = drought_stats$max_rdi,
           label = paste0("Wettest Event: ", format(drought_stats$max_date, "%b %Y"),
                          " (RDI: ", round(drought_stats$max_rdi, 2), ") •"),
           fill = "#00008B", color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5, label.size = NA, hjust = 0) +

  # Start and end of analysis period
  annotate("text", x = min(rdi_48tbl$date), y = 3, 
           label = "Start of analysis", hjust = 0.8, size = 5, color = "grey40", fontface = "bold", angle = 90) +
  annotate("text", x = max(rdi_48tbl$date), y = 3, 
           label = "End of analysis", hjust = 0.8, size = 5, color = "grey50", fontface = "bold", angle=90) +

  # Scales
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "5 years",
    date_labels = "%Y",
    limits = as.Date(c("1989-12-01", "2025-12-31")),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-3.5, 3.5),
    breaks = seq(-3.5, 3, 0.5),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(

  # Labels and theme
  labs(

    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.5),

Comparison of RDI 12 & RDI 24 & RDI 36 & RDI 48

Metric RDI 12-Month RDI 24-Month Interpretation Period 1990–2025* 1990–2025* Same base period Drought Conditions (< -0.5) 28.2% 37.6% 24-month shows more persistent dryness Severe Drought (< -1.5) 7.8% 4.7% 12-month captures sharper, shorter extremes Wet Conditions (> 0.5) 27.1% 28.9% Fairly similar in wet distribution Driest Event Jan 2019 (RDI = -3.0) Jan 2020 (RDI = -2.4) 12-month shows sharper negative anomaly Wettest Event May 1994 (RDI = 2.6) May 1995 (RDI = 3.0) Similar, offset by 1 year

✍️ Interpretation Summary: While the 24-month RDI highlights more persistent drought conditions across multi-year scales, the 12-month RDI is more sensitive to year-to-year variability, capturing sharper extremes like the 2019 drought. The higher frequency of severe drought in the 12-month scale (7.8% vs 4.7%) suggests greater short-term hydroclimatic variability, even though total wet conditions are fairly consistent across both indices.

✅ Part 2: Trend Analysis – Mann-Kendall Test

rdi_12tbl <- monthly_rdist_tbl |> 
  dplyr::select(date, RDI_12) |> 
  drop_na()
rdi_24tbl <- monthly_rdist_tbl |> 
  dplyr::select(date, RDI_24) |> 
  drop_na()
rdi_36tbl <- monthly_rdist_tbl |> 
  dplyr::select(date, RDI_36) |> 
  drop_na()
rdi_48tbl <- monthly_rdist_tbl |> 
  dplyr::select(date, RDI_48) |> 
  drop_na()

library(trend)
trend::mk.test(rdi_12tbl$RDI_12)
## 
##  Mann-Kendall trend test
## 
## data:  rdi_12tbl$RDI_12
## z = 1.133, n = 1062, p-value = 0.2572
## alternative hypothesis: true S is not equal to 0
## sample estimates:
##            S         varS          tau 
## 1.308100e+04 1.332733e+08 2.321833e-02
trend::mk.test(rdi_24tbl$RDI_24)
## 
##  Mann-Kendall trend test
## 
## data:  rdi_24tbl$RDI_24
## z = 1.7109, n = 1050, p-value = 0.08709
## alternative hypothesis: true S is not equal to 0
## sample estimates:
##            S         varS          tau 
## 1.941900e+04 1.288085e+08 3.526079e-02
trend::mk.test(rdi_36tbl$RDI_36)
## 
##  Mann-Kendall trend test
## 
## data:  rdi_36tbl$RDI_36
## z = 2.0928, n = 1038, p-value = 0.03637
## alternative hypothesis: true S is not equal to 0
## sample estimates:
##            S         varS          tau 
## 2.334700e+04 1.244445e+08 4.337954e-02
trend::mk.test(rdi_48tbl$RDI_48)
## 
##  Mann-Kendall trend test
## 
## data:  rdi_48tbl$RDI_48
## z = 2.5341, n = 1026, p-value = 0.01128
## alternative hypothesis: true S is not equal to 0
## sample estimates:
##            S         varS          tau 
## 2.778100e+04 1.201802e+08 5.283317e-02
